To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lot sizing heuritics that are based on deterministic demand are not cost effective when demand is uncertain.
lot sizing and safety stocking decisions should be based on a rolling schedule approach and that lot sizing heurists should be adapted to cope with demand uncertainties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: what is the effect of time-varying and uncertain demand on the efficiency of lot sizing and safety stocks decisions when made on a rolling schedule?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lot sizing heuristcs are not suitable for use in an MRP context with demand uncertainty.
the cost effectiveness of a lot sizing heuristic is dependent on the demand uncertainty, on the demand pattern, on the lot sizing heuristic and on the time horizon.
the lot sizing and safety stocking policies should be adapted to the characteristics of the specific situation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a single level lot sizing heuristic with safety stock is not a good idea when facing uncertain demand.
the use of safety stock is not only a means for coping with demand uncertainty, but also a means of coping with the uncertainty in the demand forecast.
a rolling schedule with a simple lot sizing heuristic is a very efficient approach to deal with demand uncertainty in MRP systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lot sizing heuritics should be applied in a rolling schedule environment.
the cost effectiveness of MRP heuristics is highly sensitive to demand variability.
the cost effectiveness of a lot sizing heuristic is strongly influenced by the demand distribution.
